properties.snippet: Kentucky Division of Water (DOW) Priority Watersheds represent watersheds where the Division intends to focus limited resources to improve water quality.
properties.description:
Division of Water (DOW) Priority Watersheds receive greater consideration for funding and technical support in state agency programs, including USEPA 319 (Nonpoint Source) Grant Program Funding, state revolving funds for water and wastewater infrastructure, and state agricultural cost-share programs. DOW Priority Watersheds are distributed throughout the state, consisting of both 319 Program Basin Priorities, and Nutrient Priorities. Each DOW Priority area is scaled to a HUC-12 watershed.

These focused investment areas consisting of both 319 Program Basin Priorities, and Nutrient Priority Areas.  Basin Priorities reflect areas with a demonstrated need for investment (impaired waters, environmental justice considerations, TMDLs, nutrient priorities, sourcewater, or local high-quality waterways), and sufficient local capacity (watershed plans) to improve water quality.  Nutrient Priorities reflect areas of high aquatic nutrient concentrations (yields), locations of repeat confirmed Harmful Algal Blooms (HABs), and sensitive drinking water sources.  Combined, these two data sets represent a data-driven prioritization effort to address specific local water quality needs.

properties.snippet: The Legacy Data Center (LDC) contains historical water quality data dating back to the early part of the 20th century and collected up to the end of 1998. STORET contains data collected beginning in 1999, along with older data that has been properly documented and migrated from the LDC. Both systems contain raw biological, chemical, and physical data on surface and ground water collected by federal, state and local agencies, Indian Tribes, volunteer groups, academics, and others. All 50 States, territories, and jurisdictions of the U.S. are represented in these systems.

candidates.title: Source Water Assessment and Protection Program Zones in Kentucky

properties.snippet: Delineated polygons show the areas that contribute drainage to the public drinking water supply and need to be protected. In Kentucky, this is the recharge area for wells or springs (Wellhead Protection Areas [WHPAs]) or the watershed upstream of surface water intakes (Source Water Assessment and Protection Program [SWAPP] zones). This data set covers surface water protection areas only; wellhead protection areas (WHPA) are a separate data set.
properties.description:
The Source Water Assessment and Protection Program (SWAPP) is designed to provide proactive planning and protection of public drinking water supplies.The SWAPP data set provides a three-tiered polygon delineation of the areas of contribution to drinking water intakes on streams, rivers, lakes and reservoirs.

Zone 1 (Critical Zone) begins ¼ mile below the intake site and extends 5 miles upstream of the intake. Zone 2 (Zone of Responsibility) extends the protection area to 10 miles above the intake. Zone 3 (Zone of Potential Impact) extends to 25 miles above the intake or to the hydrologic boundary.

This data set is published as one merged statewide data set, to show spatial extent of coverage (i.e. where protection zone 3 areas overlap, the individual polygons are merged).

candidates.title: Water Quality Certification (WQC) 401 Mitigation Sites in Kentucky

properties.snippet: The Division of Water, 401, Water Quality Certification (WQC) Program is the Commonwealth’s review and authorization of activities that require a federal license and permit, including certain permits issued by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. WQC reviews activities that may result in any discharge into the navigable waters certifying that any such discharge will comply with the state Water Quality Standards.
properties.description: The layer includes data that identifies compensatory mitigation projects in the Commonwealth. These projects are restorations of streams or wetlands performed to compensate for unavoidable impacts to streams and wetlands. The project areas are protected in perpetuity and are either under construction, monitoring post construction or have been released from monitoring and considered stable. properties.snippet: These data delineate the current primary ambient monitoring stations for the Kentucky Division of Water Ambient Rivers Monitoring program. Water quality data are collected regulary from these stations. By examining the land cover and uses of the contributing watershed, factors that contribute to water quality can be explored and addressed. These data also include nutrient (total nitrogen and total phosphorus) loads and yields data for the basins included in the study, Nutrient Loads and Yields in Kentucky: 2005-2017 and the Update to the 2019 Nutrient Loads and Yields in Kentucky Study, which includes two additional years of data.
properties.description: Primary ambient monitoring stations have ongoing water quality monitoring that oftentime extend for decades, making these stations ideal for studying water quality trends over time. The contributing basins are necessary to determine yields and understand land cover and uses that impact water quality. Contributing basins were derived using the StreamStats (USGS, 2017) web application . These data also include nutrient (total nitrogen and total phosphorus) loads and yields data for the basins included in the study, Nutrient Loads and Yields in Kentucky: 2005-2017, and the Update to the 2019 Nutrient Loads and Yields in Kentucky Study, with a study period of 2005-2019.
